rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 9 (kp 1.8, otherwise the iteration 5 baseline) is the best raced design at 432.15. Oval still finished 20 of 20 at 1.88 s. S-bend progress rose from 0.56 to 0.68, so turn authority helps the bends. Slalom did not move: progress 0.186 with exactly 1 line-loss event per run, against 0.19 in iteration 5. S-bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.36 and control effort to 8.0, so jitter is now a cost. Slalom progress has sat at about 0.186 across iterations 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9, whatever the speed, kp or line-loss mode. Only the two wider or larger variants moved it, and both made it worse: x spread ±0.07 gave 0.11 (iteration 4) and sensor_size 0.016 gave 0.12 (iteration 6).

Decision. I keep kp 1.8, since it is the best raced result and the approved fallback path for s-bend. I do not take the kp 2.0 step. Its trigger required slalom to rise above 0.19, and it did not (0.1857), while s-bend oscillation is already 0.36. For the one change this iteration, I narrow the sensor x spread from ±0.05 to ±0.04 (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04), keeping y 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, kd 0.4, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.2 and last_direction. The wider spread was the one geometry change that hurt both the oval and the slalom, so the opposite direction is the untested lever. The trade-off is that the outer sensors see less of the tape on the sharpest bends, so line loss could rise.

Expected result. Slalom progress rises above 0.19, or at least holds at about 0.19, with line_loss_events at or below 1. Oval finish stays at 1.0 and s-bend progress stays at or above about 0.6. Risk: the narrower array loses the tape earlier on the slalom, which would lower slalom progress and s-bend progress together.

Hypotheses. (a) Outer sensors at ±0.05 read the tape too late or too early on sharp bends, so the narrower spread reduces the slalom loss. (b) If slalom is unchanged, sensor geometry is not the limit, and the next test is either kd 0.5 for s-bend oscillation control or a single sensor-weight change.

Measurements wanted: per-track progress, finish rate, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation. Watch slalom progress against 0.186 and s-bend oscillation against 0.36.
